agent_messages:
I rewrote `internal/candidate/approval.go` so the batch-approval endpoint now runs through the protected `action.Executor`. It compiles, but I haven't run it against a database, so none of the audit or idempotency behaviour has been exercised. gofmt, `go vet`, `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` all pass, but no package has any tests. I didn't run `visible_smoke.py` because no independent test service was supplied, and the database credentials aren't available.

- **Setup:** `candidate.New` calls `action.New(ctx, pool, "")`, with no fault injection turned on. That call checks the Purchase RLS setup and that `ActionRequest` and `ApprovalAudit` are append-only with RLS. If either check fails, the server refuses to start.
- **The approval itself:** `Executor.BulkApprove` does all the transaction work. It locks per operation, tenant, approver and key, so concurrent requests with the same key run one at a time. It replays a stored result if the targets match and returns 409 if they don't. It approves all or nothing, and writes the audit rows, the `ActionRequest` row and its request hash in the same transaction. A failed transaction leaves nothing behind, so the same key can be retried.
- **What my code adds:** It converts `action.Rejection` into `protocol.Rejection` with the same status. Database errors pass through unchanged, so the shared adapter still turns duplicate-key errors into 409 and everything else into 503. It also turns an empty approved list into `[]` rather than `null`.
- **Identity:** The identity used comes only from the `Authorization` header, so client context headers can't override it.
- **Existing behaviour:** The old APIs, including single-item approval, are still handled by the original server and are unchanged.

I only edited `internal/candidate/`.
